text:
People Ops: Quick update on international travel: starting Aug 1 we9re introducing a mandatory preapproval flow for travel to Tier-2/Tier-3 countries + a new duty-of-care checklist. All business travel must be submitted at least 7 days before departure. Personal travel during work trips should be disclosed. Link: https://intranet.redwood.ai/policies/travel-preapprove :airplane:

Maya (HR Lead): The policy aims to speed approvals and ensure emergency support. We9ll require emergency contact, local embassy registration, and a brief business justification for audit. Town hall Thurs 4pm PT to demo the form.

Lina (Legal): Important: any travel involving sensitive client data or restricted sites must include Legal sign-off. Also watch export control rules for hardware demos. If in doubt, tag the request as `requires-legal`.

Raj (Security): Security notes: security will auto-screen destinations against our travel risk list. High-risk flags will generate a mandatory security review and possible itinerary changes. If flagged, you9ll get an email with next steps within 24h.

Olivia (Finance): Reimbursements: cash advance cap raised to $1,500 for trips over 5 days with preapproval and receipts. Per-diem defaults per-country are in the policy doc; use `travel-bot` to estimate before booking. Finance now requires the `cost-center` field in the request.

travel-bot: Tip: run `/travel-quote <dest> <days>` to get estimated per-diem and airfare band. Example: `/travel-quote DE 4`

People Ops: Quick checklist summary we9re adding to the form: purpose, client/site name, emergency contact, embassy registration (yes/no), vaccination/cert status if applicable, accommodation address, itinerary, cost-center, risk acknowledgment. If you9re on a visa, include visa type and expiry.

Maya (HR Lead): For return-to-office requirements after high-risk travel, we9ll include a health check-in workflow. If your role is eligible for quarantine pay or remote recovery, it will be in the policy.

Lina (Legal): Audit logs will capture: req_id, user, approver_chain, decision_flags, travel_country, dates, cost_center, legal_tag, timestamp. Make sure the justification field is not empty for cross-border work.

People Ops (code): Example log snippet:```
req=tr-2427506789 user=olivia approver=auto:user-manager security_flag=none country=NG start=2427600000 end=2427604320 cost_center=eng-ops ts=2427506850
```

Raj (Security): Note on NG (Nigeria) example above: security_flag would be `review` for certain regions based on current advisory. We publish the risk list to the intranet and update weekly.

Olivia (Finance): Can travel insurance be charged to the company card? We had a vendor ask.

People Ops: Short answer: preapproved business travel insurance may be charged to company card if expense is listed in the request and approved by Finance. Personal travel insurance is personal. See policy section "Insurance & Billing".

Maya (HR Lead): Managers: expect a daily digest of pending travel approvals. If you need faster handling for client-critical trips, flag `expedite` in the request and include a reason. We9ll triage expedited requests first.

travel-bot: Reminder: travel form launches Aug 1. Use `/travel-start` to begin a request.

calendar-bot: Reminder: Travel policy town hall Thurs 16:00 PT in All-Hands room + Zoom.

Raj (Security): One more: for any on-site that involves handling customer code/hardware, bring the signed NDA or C2 form. Security will verify before final approval.

People Ops: Rollout plan: Aug 1 form + bot; 2-week grace period; Aug 15 enforcement. Pilot invites for teams with frequent travel (Sales, Solutions, Research) going live today DM People Ops if you want in. Questions here or DM @People Ops.
